Crew Health in Orbit

AegisSpace is an AI system that protects astronaut health on long space missions. It monitors the crew around the clock, predicts health problems before they happen, recommends the right response, and trains the doctors who will handle those situations. Its tagline is Monitor. Predict. Protect.

The Problem

In space, an astronaut is far from any hospital, while the body is under constant strain from radiation, low gravity, isolation and psychological stress, weakened immunity, and oxygen risks. A small issue can escalate quickly. The project aims to catch danger early and reduce risk to the crew.

Prediction: An LSTM model  analyzes vitals trends and forecasts where they are heading. It raises an early warning before a reading enters the risk zone.
Protocols and approval: The system picks the best-matching protocol from a library covering low oxygen. A human supervisor approves it with one tap, and only then does the action run automatically. The final decision always stays with a person.
Simulation lab: Before anything touches the real crew, several options are tested on a digital twin of the astronaut and compared. Testing carries zero risk to the real crew.
Doctor training: The AI generates mission scenarios, a doctor responds on a virtual patient.

Project Details

What it does and how it works
AegisSpace is an AI system that protects astronaut health on long-duration missions, where medical help is far away. It works in five stages:

  1. Monitor: Sensors track vitals such as heart rate, oxygen, temperature, sleep, and breathing, along with five core space risks: radiation, low gravity, isolation stress, immunity suppression, and low oxygen.
  2. Predict: An LSTM neural network learns from vitals trends over time and forecasts where they are heading, raising an early warning before a reading enters the risk zone.
  3. Protocol and approve: The system selects the best-matching response from a protocol library (low oxygen, heart rhythm, fatigue, radiation spike). A human supervisor approves it with one tap, and only then does it run automatically.
  4. Simulate: Before anything reaches the real crew, several options are tested on a digital twin of the astronaut and compared, so the best one is applied with zero risk to the real crew.
  5. Train: The AI generates mission scenarios, a doctor responds on a virtual patient, and the AI scores the response and coaches the doctor with instant feedback.

Benefits

  • Early detection, with warnings before a condition worsens.
  • Human-approved safety, because no automated action runs without supervisor approval.
  • Safe decision-making, since options are tested on the digital twin first.
  • Better-prepared medical staff through continuous practice on realistic scenarios.

Intended impact
Healthier crews and safer missions. By shifting from reacting to emergencies to predicting them, AegisSpace aims to reduce risk on long-duration missions, where evacuation is not an option. The same approach could later support remote and isolated medical settings on Earth.

What makes it creative
Most health systems only display data. AegisSpace closes the whole loop in one system: it senses, predicts, recommends, simulates, and trains. Pairing automation with mandatory human approval, and using a digital twin as a risk-free testing ground, make it both practical and safe. Using the same AI to train the next generation of doctors adds a layer that monitoring tools usually lack.

Factors our team considered

  • Safety first: the human supervisor keeps the final decision.
  • Trust and transparency: the system suggests a protocol and shows its reasoning rather than acting on its own.
  • Isolation: the design assumes limited communication with Earth.
  • Risk-free validation: every option is tested on the digital twin before it reaches a real person.
  • Honest data: all numbers shown in our presentation are illustrative, not real medical data.
